differences.reason: The standalone context-guru proxy still hard-codes Billing{Mode: BillingAPI} for every request; it does not call accountant.BillingFrom yet (Cortex spec §5.7). Remove this entry once the context-guru proxy calls accountant.BillingFrom. Not a case in github.com/rossoctl/accountant/test/cases, so this is a documentation-only note rather than a skip for TestAccountantCases.

Shadow (Cortex design §6, accountant wiring W9 'expected differences'): the accountant's PenaltyUSD for a rewrite inside the cached prefix is the tokens the provider actually re-wrote, from the read extent. The figure it is compared with used the whole cache_write as an upper bound, so the new penalty is lower. The figure before the switch (settle.Avoided, removed in Task 9) carried no penalty at all, so the ledger's penaltyMicros starts from 0.

Shadow (W9; accountant design §6.2): the tier of each change comes from its position against the cache boundary (cache read before B*, write or input after it). The figure before the switch (settle.Avoided, removed in Task 9) priced tool-prune's saving by a byte-to-token ratio over the whole prompt and put all of it in the one tier pricing.AvoidedUsage picks for the request. The two agree only when every removed tool sits on one side of the boundary.

W9: the context_guru_expand declaration the context-guru proxy injects is a cost (a rewrite that adds bytes) in the accountant's figure; the current figure does not count it. In Cortex the plugin has no expand loop (OnResponse is a pass-through), so the declaration is not injected and this applies to the proxy arm of the cross-host harness only.
W9; accountant design §6.2: a cache-break penalty starts at the read extent (what the provider still read), not at the break position. With few breakpoints it is larger than a count from the break.

W9: a keep-alive window whose pings rescued nothing is a negative figure for its thread. Cortex keeps a ping's spend in its own cost record (Purpose keep-alive, design §5.8), which the ledger and /v1/usage count in keepAliveMicros and keepAlivePings, never in costMicros or requests; the keeper's event.Saving holds only the rescue, in avoidedMicros. The two are not netted per thread, so a window that rescued nothing shows as keep-alive spend with no keeper saving, not as one negative figure.

Accountant wiring W7.1 (one Saving per operator) and W9 step 8; Cortex design §6 (shadow agreement, ledger before and after the switch). The figure before the switch (settle.Avoided, removed in Task 9) priced tool-prune only (settle.savingComponents). Every context-guru operator (context-guru.*) and the keeper appear only in the accountant's figure, so after the switch each adds to the ledger's avoidedMicros and penaltyMicros against 0 before it.

Cortex threads the accountant by subagent: "main" for the primary agent and the Claude Code subagent id otherwise (core/accounting.ThreadOf, wiring W5.2). The context-guru proxy sets context-guru's Opts.ThreadOf, which splits threads by prefix continuity inside the engine. Cortex does not wire Opts.ThreadOf, so res.Trace.Thread.ID is empty and the plugin's SetAccountingThread is a no-op. Two requests the proxy puts on different threads (or one thread) can be one thread (or two) in Cortex, so per-thread Tracker state, and the boundary and breaks it yields, can differ.

Accountant wiring W5.2 (threads); Cortex design §5.4. The context-guru plugin passes the engine's fork origin (Trace.Thread.InheritsFrom, 'Inherits') as accountant.Thread.Parent; with no ThreadOf wired it is empty, and the default rule's Parent is the Claude Code parent subagent, else "main". The proxy's Parent comes from its own thread key. A forked thread's first request can therefore inherit a different parent's state in the two hosts.

Cortex does not compute EntryFacts.SharedWarm (it never calls accountant.SharedWarmFrom over sibling threads' forwarded bodies). The proxy does (proxy/accountant_savings.go, siblingStore). A thread whose first request reads a prefix another thread of the session warmed is therefore not marked shared-warm in Cortex, and the library may read its cache read as a different phase. Accountant design §5.2 (shared warm) / check shared_warm.

Accountant wiring W7.1 (Event.UnattributedBreakUSD; a break with no ChangeID); accountant design §6.3. Cortex's Event.UnattributedBreakUSD (core/accounting.Savings) is the net cost of every non-InBaseline cache effect no applied op owns: a break with no ChangeID (a change that had ended), one whose ChangeID only a dry run reported, and a split, TTL or mark effect with no owning op; the W7.1 name is kept although it holds more than breaks. InBaseline effects are skipped entirely. The proxy (dash/accountant_price.go) puts InBaseline and dry-run-owned breaks in its UnattributedBreakUSD (shown, not counted) and the ended-change break in EndedBreakUSD, which it counts in the request's delta. So the unattributed figures of the two hosts hold different breaks; the per-operator figures do not differ.

Accountant wiring W7.1 (cache effects settled by Kind); accountant design §4.4. Cortex books a split, ttlPremium, ttlRescue, markPremium or markPayback effect to the operator of the applied op with its ChangeID, as USD when its Net prices positive and PenaltyUSD when negative, and to UnattributedBreakUSD when no op owns it. The proxy books split and headttl effects in their own rows (SplitUSD, TTLUSD) and an unowned markPremium/markPayback to the tailbreakpoint row. Totals agree; the per-operator rows can differ.

Accountant wiring W6.4 (envelope changes); Cortex design §6 (cross-host). When tool-prune runs before context-guru in the outbound chain, the context-guru plugin's envelope ops (core/plugins/contextguru/envelope.go) diff the body tool-prune left against the body it writes, so the tool indexes they name are post-tool-prune positions, while the accountant indexes ops against the client body. The context-guru proxy sees no tool-prune and indexes against the client body. The bytes and tokens of each op are the same; only the tier can differ, and only when the cache boundary B* falls inside the tools section, so that a shifted index lands on the other side of it.

Accountant wiring W6.1 (upstream_rounds); Cortex design §5.9. A request that took more than one upstream round (the inference-router's resend) has no accountant figure, so after the switch it carries no saving; before it, settle.Avoided priced tool-prune's removal from the bytes removed. The context-guru proxy skips the same requests, so this is a difference from the old ledger, not from the proxy.

Cortex design §5.3: with accounting off (accounting.enabled false, or auto with no context operator in the outbound chain), no saving is recorded after the switch. Before it, settle.Avoided priced a tool-prune saving whether or not the accountant ran.

Cortex design §5.7a (money totals count only basis usd). A saving recorded before the switch has no basis, so the totals folded from session events (the sessions list, a usage ring replayed from the session archive) no longer count it. Ledger rows written before the switch keep their avoidedMicros, and read penaltyMicros and the other new columns as 0.
